Expected Calibration Error (ECE) at a Single Time Point

Source: R/evaluation.R
ece_survmat.Rd

Computes a binned Expected Calibration Error at time t_star, using quantile-based bins of predicted survival probabilities.

Usage

ece_survmat(object, sp_matrix, t_star, n_bins = 10L, p = 1, weighted = TRUE)

Arguments

object

A Surv object.

sp_matrix

Matrix or data frame of survival probabilities with rows = subjects and (optionally) columns named "t=<time>".

t_star

Numeric evaluation time (must be a single value).

n_bins

Integer number of quantile bins (default 10).

p

Power for the L^p error (default 1 gives absolute error).

weighted

Logical; if TRUE (default) weights bin errors by n_k / N where n_k is the bin size.

Value

A named numeric scalar: "ece".

Details

Let \(\hat{S}_k(t^*)\) be the mean predicted survival in bin \(k\) and \(\tilde{S}_k(t^*)\) the Kaplan-Meier survival at \(t^*\) in that bin. The (weighted) ECE is $$ \mathrm{ECE}(t^*) = \left( \sum_k w_k \, |\hat{S}_k(t^*) - \tilde{S}_k(t^*)|^p \right)^{1/p} $$ with \(w_k = n_k / N\).

See also

The calibration curve is available as interpret(fit, method = "calibration") (via compute_calibration()); ece_survmat() is the scalar summary of the same idea used by evaluate(metrics = "ece").

Examples

y <- survival::Surv(
  time = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9),
  event = c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0)
)
sp <- cbind("t=5" = c(0.15, 0.20, 0.35, 0.40, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.80))
ece_survmat(y, sp_matrix = sp, t_star = 5, n_bins = 4)
#>     ece 
#> 0.29375
